mbm-2126.clue: I put a lift in the biscuit tin.
mbm-2126.quote: I wrote a tiny simulation of the bus station lifts. My uncle wanted something more cheerful to ride in them, so we scanned in his biscuit collection. A custard cream now commutes to the second floor.

mbm-2127.clue: My running shoes have a second finish line.
mbm-2127.quote: At home I slide them under a low bench after each run. One lace always hangs out. My little cousin puts a ribbon across the gap so they can finish the race without me.

mbm-2128.clue: I paddle back for the lost sound.
mbm-2128.quote: Under our low wooden bridge the canoe rings like a hollow drum when I tap its rim. My friend and I went back three times to get one short tune right.

mbm-2129.clue: I draw the monster's lunch first.
mbm-2129.quote: Our animation club each invented a monster. Mine had a packed lunch tied in a checked cloth. A club member drew the three-year-old monster who packed it for him. Now he's a father.

mbm-2130.clue: I made my first route out of refrigerator magnets.
mbm-2130.quote: While a sprained ankle kept me at home, I copied my climbing wall with colorful magnets. My brother moved my tiny paper climber up the fridge until I could finish the real thing.

mbm-2131.clue: My pencil plane flies only in shadow.
mbm-2131.quote: I carved a little wing onto my drawing pencil. If I hold it up beside the airfield fence, its shadow lines up with the planes waiting to take off. That's my fleet of one.

mbm-2132.clue: I'm mending a memory the color of peaches.
mbm-2132.quote: A strip of my grandmother's peach apron ran through her first quilt. Near the edge it's almost white from hands pulling it up. I matched new thread to the faded part.

mbm-2133.clue: I took a swimming lesson from a leaf.
mbm-2133.quote: A little leaf floated along the outside lane while I practiced backstroke. I tried to keep my shoulders as quiet as its reflection. It beat me to the flags by an inch.

mbm-2134.clue: My pages sometimes need real shoelaces.
mbm-2134.quote: I tied two handwritten chapters together with a green lace because I'd run out of clips. My hero spent the whole next chapter looking for his left shoe.

mbm-2135.clue: The patch faces me when I hang it up.
mbm-2135.quote: My first martial arts uniform has a round patch I sewed on backward. In the changing-room mirror it looks just right. I keep it hanging by my good one for luck.

mbm-2136.clue: My kayak draws a long green line.
mbm-2136.quote: I filmed a sunset paddle from the footbridge. You barely see the little boat, only my bright green blade flicking in and out of the frame. My mum recognized the stroke.

mbm-2137.clue: I kept the squeak in the recording.
mbm-2137.quote: I recorded a duet with an old friend in his kitchen. His chair squeaked between verses. He passed me the clean take, but the squeak is how I know when to come in.

mbm-2138.clue: The red tree is our halfway mark.
mbm-2138.quote: My favorite frisbee throw turns just past a maple. In autumn the red disc disappears for a beat in the leaves. I wait for my friend's grin to know it came out the other side.

mbm-2139.clue: I stick to the short pass in the biscuit game.
mbm-2139.quote: We balance an empty biscuit tin on a fence post and try to brush the rim with a disc. When it rings, the thrower gets the last biscuit. Last week the wind won.

mbm-2140.clue: My hardest button goes on a book.
mbm-2140.quote: I made a fabric cover for Mum's recipe book and sewed on a big red button. Her hands are usually floury, so I braided the loop from a thick shoelace. She closes it with an elbow.

mbm-2141.quote: I crocheted a strip of bright yarn for each town on my best friend's journey. Folded twice, the strip became a potholder. She can put supper down on exactly where she is.

mbm-2142.clue: My neatest vine goes up a sleeve.
mbm-2142.quote: I laid my aunt's pollera sleeve flat to embroider a green vine. On the table it looked like the straightest row I'd ever stitched. Then she tried it on and turned her wrist. The leaves went around her like a bracelet.

mbm-2143.clue: We play one point for the picnic ants.
mbm-2143.quote: My friends and I move our frisbee target a little to the left if the ants are busy. The day we hit it from the new spot they were already carrying off a victory crumb.

mbm-2144.clue: I carry the long rest in my coat pocket.
mbm-2144.quote: Our choir conductor gave me a pebble for every beat of a tricky rest. I rolled them across my palm in rehearsal. When I sang that entry on time, I gave the pebbles to the next nervous singer.

mbm-2145.quote: I rehearse folding shirts. A low note makes the loose handle on the wicker basket buzz, so I can tell when I've found my part. My partner heard it and joined the harmony.

mbm-2146.clue: The last level has my mother's wallpaper.
mbm-2146.quote: I made a paper cover for the back of our television so my brother and I could pretend the final boss lived behind it. Mum donated a scrap of kitchen wallpaper. Now the villain lives near an excellent sink.

mbm-2147.clue: I judge the turn by the red hat.
mbm-2147.quote: My cousin wears a red hat in the tow boat so I can spot her in the spray. On my first smooth turn she lifted it over her head and I forgot all about watching my feet.

mbm-2148.clue: There's a quiet side to the bell.
mbm-2148.quote: At the outdoor bath you hear the far temple bell only after the wind drops. I was folding my towel when it finally rang. I sat back on the warm rock and listened to the last little note.

mbm-2149.clue: I made a cup for the edge of the table.
mbm-2149.quote: Our kitchen table has a little groove worn by years of elbows. I shaped the foot of a cup to sit perfectly flat there. That's Dad's place, even if we rearrange the chairs.

mbm-2150.clue: I stitched the red square twice.
mbm-2150.quote: My sister moved house midway through our quilt project. I put a little red door on both ends of the blanket and stitched a blue line between them. It fits her new sofa perfectly.
